checks.claim: C1a: Section 1 matches canonical H:homog in dimensions, threshold, homogeneity, measure class and spectral convention.
checks.reason: The note has d in {1,2,3}, a=alpha_0 in (0,1), alpha+a<2, and 0<alpha<d or alpha=d=1. It also has Gamma(cA)=c^(d-alpha)Gamma(A) and Gamma=int exp(i xi.x) mu(dxi) distributionally, all agreeing with the excerpt. Sanity check: for d=1 and Gamma=delta_0, mu=dxi/(2pi), and (1) reduces to phi(0)=phi(0) by inversion.

checks.claim: C1b: The nonzero assumption and zero boundary are handled honestly, and singular spectra are covered.
checks.reason: H:homog does not state nonzero. The note adds it explicitly and Section 6 says it is excluded only to make M_Gamma>0. For Gamma=0, mu=0 and (2),(3),(5),(6) hold trivially with zero constants. No step uses a density of mu. rho_R is a density of the auxiliary measure only.

checks.claim: C1c: A tempered positive measure integrates Schwartz functions absolutely, by the polynomial mass argument.
checks.reason: Seminorms of phi(x/R) satisfy p_m(phi(./R))<=R^m p_m(phi) for R>=1, so ball mass grows polynomially. Dyadic shells then give integrability of (1+|x|)^(-N) for large N. This is correct for Gamma and mu. Identifying the distribution pairing with the Lebesgue integral on non-compact Schwartz tests (cutoffs plus dominated convergence) is left implicit. It is standard and non-blocking.

checks.claim: C1d: Identity (1) and the unitary Fourier convention are exact and consistent for complex tests.
checks.reason: (1) is the definition of the Fourier transform of the tempered measure mu, extended bilinearly to complex tests. hat f has constant c_d=(2pi)^(-d/2) and sign exp(-i xi.x), and all later constants were rechecked against this.

checks.claim: C2a: Identity (2) holds for all y and r>0 with exact constants, and uses no illegal oscillatory Fubini.
checks.reason: J'(b)=-b J(b)/(2A) was rederived by parts. With A=r^2/4, J=(2 sqrt(pi)/r)exp(-b^2/r^2). Applying (1) to the single test exp(-r^2|x|^2/4)exp(-i y.x) gives (2) directly, and no exchange of two infinite measures is performed.

checks.claim: C2b: The homogeneity pushforward and the bounds in (3) are correct, including C_Gamma.
checks.reason: T(x)=rx gives T_#Gamma(A)=Gamma(A/r)=r^(alpha-d)Gamma(A), hence int exp(-r^2|x|^2/4)dGamma=r^(alpha-d)M_Gamma. So G_r(y)<=r^alpha M_Gamma/(2 sqrt(pi))^d. On open or closed B(y,r) the Gaussian is >=1/e, giving mu(B(y,r))<=e M_Gamma r^alpha/(2 sqrt(pi))^d=C_Gamma r^alpha uniformly in y and r. Hand checks: Gamma=delta_0 in d=1 and delta_x1 tensor Leb_x2 in d=2 satisfy it, with C_Gamma=e/(2 sqrt(pi)) in the latter.

checks.claim: C3a: R scaling, L, and evenness of |k_R| hold for a real, not necessarily even, mask.
checks.reason: k_R(u)=R^d hat zeta(Ru), so ||k_R||_1=L, and L>0 because zeta is nonzero. Real zeta gives k_R(-u)=conj k_R(u), so |k_R| is even. With evenness of mu and xi->-xi, rho_R(-eta)=rho_R(eta).

checks.claim: C3b: rho_R is finite and continuous, and nu_R is positive, Radon and tempered.
checks.reason: Rapid decay of k_R with the polynomial mass of mu gives finiteness. On compact eta sets (1+|xi-eta|)^(-N)<=C_K(1+|xi|)^(-N), so dominated convergence gives continuity. A continuous nonnegative density yields a positive Radon measure, and temperedness follows from (5) plus dyadic shells. The note correctly says local density bounds need not be uniform in R; the Gaussian example has density proportional to R.

checks.claim: C3c: The Tonelli shifted-center identity and the uniform bound (5) hold with constant c_d^2 L^2 C_Gamma.
checks.reason: For fixed xi and u=xi-eta, eta in B(y,r) iff xi in B(y+u,r), with unit Jacobian. This gives nu_R(B(y,r))=c_d^2 L int |k_R(u)| mu(B(y+u,r))du. Then (3) and int |k_R|=L give (5), uniformly in R, y and r.

checks.claim: C4a: The Hilbert-valued convolution identity with constant c_d holds, with valid integrability and projection limits.
checks.reason: The scalar computation gives hat(fg)=c_d hat f * hat g. Coordinates of H-valued Schwartz functions are scalar Schwartz, and hat(P_n F)=P_n hat F. Pointwise convergence is dominated by |zeta_R| ||F|| on one side and |k_R(xi-eta)| ||hat F(eta)|| on the other. hat F decays rapidly in norm by Bochner differentiation. Continuity in a separable H gives strong measurability.

checks.claim: C4b: Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz and Tonelli give (6) exactly, with real H handled by complexification.

Integrating against mu and applying Tonelli gives int ||hat F||^2 rho_R deta exactly. Finiteness follows from temperedness. A real H embeds isometrically in H_C with the usual norm.

minor: Line 287 says Proposition 2 'enlarges the norm of INPUT TESTS'. Read as an order statement this is false, since N_R need not dominate the original norm. In the d=2 example with a Gaussian mask, take hat f(eta)=a(eta1)b(eta2/eps) with a,b real even Schwartz and b(0)=1. The original spatial variance is 2pi||a||^2, independent of eps, while N_R^2<=C_R eps->0. Proposition 3 excludes the reverse domination, so the two norms are incomparable here. 'Replaces' would be accurate. The proof only uses the masked map on A_R and never uses W(F) on A_R, so nothing fails.

Line 286 says Proposition 3 forbids importing the old d1 estimate 'to all d2/3 covariances', but Proposition 3 is a d=2 example only. It refutes the universal d=2 claim directly. A d=3 instance is not written. The analogue delta_0(dx1) tensor Leb(dx2 dx3), alpha=1, g=chi(x1)chi''(x2)chi(x3), works by the same marginal argument, but the note does not state it. The old d1 estimate itself is outside the packet.

Lines 173-175 do not state why Schwartz-in-space tests in D lie in the canonical completion if W is initially given on compact tests. Spatial cutoffs converge in Schwartz topology and (7) is continuous in Schwartz seminorms, so this is a one-line remark. The packet excerpt does not fix a narrower test class.

Section 1 leaves implicit that the tempered pairing on non-compact Schwartz tests coincides with the Lebesgue integral (cutoff plus dominated convergence). This is standard, and the Gaussian tests in Section 2 rely on it.
